messages.subject: Re: No applicable method for 'xtable' applied to an object of class "c('double', 'numeric')"
parts:
The second error looks familiar, and I guess you need to upgrade
RStudio: http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/preview/

For the first error, I'd recommend you to print() the last expression
inside renderTable() to see if it is really a data frame or matrix. My
guess is that you have got a numeric vector somehow:

> xtable::xtable(1:10)
Error in UseMethod("xtable") :
no applicable method for 'xtable' applied to an object of class

"c('integer', 'numeric')"

When you index a data frame or matrix, make sure to use drop = FALSE
to prevent R from accidentally dropping the 2D data structure into 1D,
e.g. x[, j, drop = FALSE].

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: No applicable method for 'xtable' applied to an object of class "c('double', 'numeric')"
parts:
David, I had the same issue but I was using renderTable(). Apparently, after some research I found that this was so because the renderTable() option accepts a tabular format.
Therefore I fixed this issue by using  z <- x[, y, drop = FALSE]  (x being the data frame and y the desired column) to ensure a tabular structure  which I then pass to the renderTable().
Hopefully that helps.

parts:
OK, a few problems here:

You had this snippet of code:

    read.table(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep,
             quote=input$quote)

    df=as.data.frame(inFile)

read.table returns the data frame you want, but you're throwing it away and substituting it with as.data.frame(inFrame) which doesn't make sense. You want this:

    df <- read.table(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep,
             quote=input$quote)

Also, it seems like you have a pretty specific data format you're expecting. I wouldn't bother with letting the header, sep, and quote variables be customizable by the end-user:

    df <- read.table(inFile$datapath, header=FALSE, sep="\t", quote="")

(and remove the corresponding input controls from ui.R)

At the end of your renderTable(), you've just got "counttotbeneficial" and "counttotdetrimental" values, each of which is a single number; how do you want these to be presented as a table? Are you sure it's even a table that you want?
